Maintenance Report — MNT-0133-007

Asset: WELL-0133 (NE-07 Well 133, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 10 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 10 May 2024 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 13 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0133-0081 on 2024-05-09 Report written: 11 May 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0133-0081 at 14:45 on 2024-05-09 found crude oil on the pad: about 3.0% of the pad area, estimated 0.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 240 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 192 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0133-007 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.82% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit

Maintenance Report — MNT-0133-016

Asset: WELL-0133 (NE-07 Well 133, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 29 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 10 Sep 2025 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 288 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0133-0148 on 2025-08-28 Report written: 11 Sep 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0133-0148 showed the wellhead at 36.4 °C with the air at 34.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 10 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0133-020

Asset: WELL-0133 (NE-07 Well 133, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 25 Apr 2026 08:00 · Finished: 19 May 2026 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 581 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0133-0182 on 2026-04-23 Report written: 19 May 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0133-0182 showed the wellhead at 23.6 °C with the air at 20.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD

Bolts, shims and seals415
Bearing grease and consumables691

Total5,094

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

Triggered by: inspection INS-0133-0190 on 2026-06-25 Report written: 27 Jun 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0133-0190 at 09:00 on 2026-06-25 found crude oil on the pad: about 2.2% of the pad area, estimated 1.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.9 hours after the inspection.
